evidence_items.publisher: Kent K. Chang and colleagues, arXiv

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI models, and GPT-4 in particular, have memorized a wide collection of in-copyright books.

evidence_items.explanation: The study supplies empirical evidence of copyrighted material in particular OpenAI models. Its scope cannot establish the proportion across all LLMs, so it is context for the population claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: For Terms of Service crawling restrictions, a full 45% of C4 is now restricted.

evidence_items.explanation: The audit documents material restrictions affecting access to web training data, supporting the data-pressure component. It does not measure how many models contain copyrighted works or prove that scarcity caused their use.

receipt.public_excerpt: If trends continue, language models will fully utilize this stock between 2026 and 2032

evidence_items.explanation: This contemporaneous estimate places full use of the available text stock in the future under stated assumptions. It cautions against interpreting desperate as already having exhausted all data, while remaining compatible with current access pressure.

unresolved_gaps: No representative model census or audit establishes the overwhelming-majority prevalence asserted.
Many examples from a few model families cannot supply the missing denominator.
The severity of current data pressure is not defined.
The suggested causal connection between scarcity and copyrighted-data use remains unestablished.
